title: Monsters of myth
summary: Three creatures from Greek myth come to life from your art. Skylla, the sea witch of the monster signals, is now the reference picture itself, cut into a rig - tentacles writhing, hair drifting, arms clawing - and fights with a tentacle sweep and an ink cloud that drags you to a crawl in darkness. The Minotaur is the main quest's new final boss at the heart of the Labyrinth, with bull rushes, twin eye beams and a shield-draining pulse. Cerberus joins the monster signals, fire pouring from all three jaws. Every creature now dies in a shaking, bursting death with a huge explosion while the camera watches. All of it was playtested and tuned to the kill. The scanner's signal paths now fade from the signal toward you, and out-of-range signals are hidden from the maps. The Library gained a MONSTERS room.

steps.title: Signal paths, by the signal
steps.text: The scanner's paths to located signals are brightest at the signal and fade toward your ship, gone a third of the system across from it (about 7,300 in Atrapos): from farther away, the end near you is clear. The light pulses along them glide four times slower, and the glow falls off smoothly in six fine layers. Out of that range a signal isn't shown on the radar or the system map at all.

steps.title: Skylla, traced from her art
steps.text: Skylla, the sea witch of the monster signals, is no longer redrawn in code: she is your reference art itself, its background removed with an anime-tuned cut-out model and split into six parts - the tentacle cluster, the upper body and each arm as an upper arm and a forearm with the clawed hand. In the game they're put together as in the undivided picture, her body seated deep in the tentacles. Shaders make the tentacles writhe and her hair drift, her arms swing at shoulders and elbows, and the pieces overlap 30 px at every joint so bending never shows a gap. She stays upright on screen as drawn.

diagram.text: every line, shape and colour of the picture kept

steps.title: Skylla's own attacks
steps.text: Playtested with the starting ship, Skylla died in 22 seconds. Now she has 2,800 hull and 800 shields that recover, her orbs are pink and magenta, and she has two attacks of her own. The tentacle sweep: a red arc of her reach follows you for 0.8 seconds, then her tentacles lash across it for 30 damage and throw you back. The ink: she spits a blob at where you were; it bursts into a cloud that lasts 6 seconds, and inside it your ship crawls at 40 % speed while the whole view goes almost black. The fight now lasts about 75 seconds. The boss's name no longer overlaps the system's.

steps.title: The Minotaur, the last boss
steps.text: The main quest gets a final boss: at the heart of the Labyrinth, after Talos, a ring of gold blazes and the Minotaur rises - the true Asterion, whose name the pirate warlord of chapter 4 only borrowed. He's cut from your art like Skylla - his body with the gold ring and its starfield, both arms and the kicking leg - and his red cape ripples. Beating him pays 2,500 credits, 3 data cores and 5 alien alloy before the archive's ending; four new lines are voiced.

steps.title: The Minotaur's weapons
steps.text: Playtested to the kill: with the starting ship he first died in 39 seconds. Now he has 5,000 hull and 1,500 recovering shields, and a rotation of attacks: bullet-hell orbs from his eyes; the bull rush - an arrow follows you, then he charges where you were; twin beams from his eyes that track you while he aims, then fire fixed along that line for 1.8 seconds, drawn on top of him; and a golden pulse that kills your shields for 4 seconds before they come back. Below half hull his orbs speed up and he rushes more. The fight now lasts about 2 3/4 minutes.

steps.title: A death to remember
steps.text: Every creature now dies hard: it shakes for 2.4 seconds, harder and harder, flickering red-hot with explosions bursting across its body, then goes up in a very large explosion with four more round it. Meanwhile the camera glides over to watch and returns to your ship afterwards - only the creature shakes. The quest moves on, and the signal's loot drops, after the explosion.

steps.title: Cerberus, and a room for monsters
steps.text: Cerberus, the three-headed hound, joins the monster signals - each signal is either Skylla or Cerberus, always the same one for that signal. He's cut from your art the same way (the background glow inside his tail's arc cleaned out): his side heads snap out of step, his legs paw and his tail lashes, and his fire comes from all three jaws in turn. The Library has a new MONSTERS room with every creature alive: Skylla, the Minotaur, Cerberus and the Void Leviathan.

+	_rig = Node2D.new()
+	_rig.scale = Vector2.ONE * art_scale
+	add_child(_rig)
+	var hub := _v(meta["hub"])
+	_body = Node2D.new()
+	_rig.add_child(_body)
+	# The limbs behind? No - in front: they run on under the body at the joint,
+	# so they go on top and the body fills in behind when they swing.
+	var body := _part("body", hub)
+	var cm := ShaderMaterial.new()
+	cm.shader = CAPE_SHADER
+	cm.set_shader_parameter("cape_mask", load("res://data/masks/monster_minotaur_cape.png"))
+	cm.set_shader_parameter("tex_size", body.texture.get_size())
+	cm.set_shader_parameter("time_offset", randf() * 100.0)
+	body.material = cm
+	_body.add_child(body)
+	for limb in ["left_leg", "left_arm", "right_arm"]:
+		var piv := _v(meta[limb + "_pivot"])
+		var joint := Node2D.new()
+		joint.position = piv - hub
+		_body.add_child(joint)
+		joint.add_child(_part(limb, piv))
+		_limbs[limb] = joint
+	_fx = Node2D.new()
+	_fx.draw.connect(_draw_fx)
+	_body.add_child(_fx)
+	# On top of all of him: the beams, the shockwave and the rush's path.
+	_over = Node2D.new()
+	_over.draw.connect(_draw_over)
+	add_child(_over)
+
+
+func _v(a: Array) -> Vector2:
+	return Vector2(float(a[0]), float(a[1]))
+
+
+func _part(part: String, origin: Vector2) -> Sprite2D:
+	var s := Sprite2D.new()
+	s.name = part
+	s.texture = load(ART + "_" + part + ".png")
+	s.centered = false
+	s.position = _v(meta["parts"][part]) - origin
+	s.texture_filter = CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS
+	return s
+
+
+## The art (1254 px square round his chest), upright.
+func visual_size() -> Vector2:
+	return Vector2(length, length) * 1.43
+
+
+## One of his eyes (0, 1) in world space: his orbs and beams come from them.
+func eye(i: int) -> Vector2:
+	if meta.is_empty() or _body == null:
+		return super.mouth()
+	return _rig.to_global(_v(meta["eyes"][i]) - _v(meta["hub"]) + _body.position)
+
+
+## Between his eyes: where the attacks aim from.
+func mouth() -> Vector2:
+	if meta.is_empty() or _body == null:
+		return super()
+	return (eye(0) + eye(1)) * 0.5
+
+
+## 0..1: winding up an attack (or a rush), for the look.
+func _charge() -> float:
+	if demo:
+		return smoothstep(0.55, 0.85, sin(_t * 0.7))
+	if _rush >= 0.0 or special != "":
+		return 1.0
+	if pattern == "":
+		return 0.0
+	return clampf(1.0 + _pt / CHARGE, 0.0, 1.0) if _pt < 0.0 else 1.0
+
+
+## Dying: stop whatever he was doing first.
+func death_throes() -> void:
+	_rush = -1.0
+	special = ""
+	await super()
+
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	if enemy and is_instance_valid(enemy) and phase == 1 and enemy.hull < enemy.max_hull * 0.5:
+		phase = 2
+		Sfx.play_world("space/monster_roar", global_position, 0.0, 0.05)
+		GameLog.post("The Minotaur roars - he's enraged!", "danger")
+	if dying:
+		_t += delta
+	elif _rush >= 0.0:
+		_t += delta
+		_run_rush(delta)
+	elif special != "":
+		_t += delta
+		_run_special(delta)
+	else:
+		var was := pattern
+		super(delta)
+		if was == "" and pattern != "":   # a new attack began: which one is up?
+			var seq: Array = SEQUENCE if phase == 1 else SEQUENCE_2
+			var kind: String = seq[_attacks % seq.size()]
+			_attacks += 1
+			if kind != "orbs" and _target() != null:
+				pattern = ""
+				if kind == "rush":
+					_rush = 0.0
+					_rush_hit = false
+					Sfx.play_world("space/monster_roar", global_position, -4.0, 0.1)
+				else:
+					special = kind
+					_sp = 0.0
+					_pulse_r = -1.0
+					_pulse_hit = false
+					var tgt := _target()
+					_beam_ang = (tgt.global_position - mouth()).angle()
+	_update_pulse(delta)
+	if _rig == null:
+		return
+	_rig.global_rotation = 0.0
+	var charge := _charge()
+	_body.position = Vector2(sin(_t * 0.9) * 5.0, sin(_t * 1.4) * 5.0 + charge * 14.0) / art_scale
+	_body.scale = Vector2.ONE * (1.0 + 0.01 * sin(_t * 1.6))
+	var swing := sin(_t * 1.25)
+	_limbs["left_arm"].rotation = 0.09 * swing - 0.25 * charge
+	_limbs["right_arm"].rotation = -0.08 * sin(_t * 1.25 + 1.6) + 0.18 * charge
+	_limbs["left_leg"].rotation = 0.06 * sin(_t * 1.1 + 0.8) + 0.12 * charge
+	_fx.queue_redraw()
+	_over.queue_redraw()
+	queue_redraw()
+
+
+## The bull rush: wind up (facing you), then charge straight on.
+func _run_rush(delta: float) -> void:
+	var tgt := _target()
+	_rush += delta
+	if _rush < RUSH_WINDUP:
+		if tgt:   # following you; when he charges, it's at the spot you were in
+			_rush_dir = (tgt.global_position - enemy.global_position).normalized()
+		return
+	if _rush < RUSH_WINDUP + RUSH_TIME and enemy and is_instance_valid(enemy):
+		enemy.global_position += _rush_dir * RUSH_SPEED * delta
+		if tgt and not _rush_hit and tgt.global_position.distance_to(enemy.global_position) < length * 0.3 + float(tgt.get("hit_radius")):
+			_rush_hit = true
+			tgt.take_damage(RUSH_DAMAGE, enemy.global_position, enemy)
+		return
+	_rush = -1.0
+	rushes += 1
+	_cool = PAUSE * (0.7 if phase == 2 else 1.0)
+
+
+## The beam and the pulse.
+func _run_special(delta: float) -> void:
+	var tgt := _target()
+	_sp += delta
+	match special:
+		"beam":
+			if _sp <= BEAM_WINDUP:   # aiming: following you
+				if tgt:
+					_beam_ang = (tgt.global_position - mouth()).angle()
+			elif tgt:   # firing: fixed where you were - it doesn't follow
+				var dir := Vector2.from_angle(_beam_ang)
+				for i in 2:   # a beam from each eye
+					var from := eye(i)
+					var rel: Vector2 = tgt.global_position - from
+					var along := rel.dot(dir)
+					if along > 0.0 and along < BEAM_LENGTH and absf(rel.cross(dir)) < BEAM_WIDTH + float(tgt.get("hit_radius")) * 0.5:

+			if _sp > BEAM_WINDUP + BEAM_TIME:
+				_end_special()
+		"pulse":
+			if _sp >= PULSE_WINDUP and _pulse_r < 0.0:
+				_pulse_r = 0.0
+				Sfx.play_world("space/monster_roar", global_position, -2.0, 0.2)
+			if _sp > PULSE_WINDUP + 0.2:
+				_end_special()
+
+
+## The shockwave keeps rolling out after he's moved on to the next attack.
+func _update_pulse(delta: float) -> void:
+	if _pulse_r < 0.0:
+		return
+	_pulse_r += PULSE_SPEED * delta
+	var tgt := _target()
+	if tgt and not _pulse_hit and enemy and is_instance_valid(enemy) and absf(tgt.global_position.distance_to(enemy.global_position) - _pulse_r) < 40.0:
+		_pulse_hit = true
+		if tgt.has_method("drain_shields"):
+			tgt.drain_shields(DRAIN_TIME)
+	if _pulse_r > PULSE_REACH:
+		_pulse_r = -1.0
+
+
+func _end_special() -> void:
+	specials_done[special] = int(specials_done.get(special, 0)) + 1
+	special = ""
+	_cool = PAUSE * (0.7 if phase == 2 else 1.0)
+
+
+## Above his art: the twin beams from his eyes, the pulse, the rush's path.
+func _draw_over() -> void:
+	# The beam (world -> local), its warning line while he aims.
+	if special == "beam":
+		for i in 2:   # twin beams, one from each eye
+			var from := to_local(eye(i))
+			var to := to_local(eye(i) + Vector2.from_angle(_beam_ang) * BEAM_LENGTH)
+			if _sp < BEAM_WINDUP:
+				_over.draw_line(from, to, Color(1.0, 0.2, 0.15, 0.25 + 0.4 * (_sp / BEAM_WINDUP)), 2.0, true)
+			else:
+				var flick := 1.0 + 0.15 * sin(_t * 50.0 + i)
+				_over.draw_line(from, to, Color(1.0, 0.25, 0.1, 0.18), BEAM_WIDTH * 1.8 * flick, true)
+				_over.draw_line(from, to, Color(1.0, 0.45, 0.2, 0.55), BEAM_WIDTH * 0.8 * flick, true)
+				_over.draw_line(from, to, Color(1.0, 0.95, 0.8, 0.95), BEAM_WIDTH * 0.25, true)
+				_over.draw_circle(from, BEAM_WIDTH * 0.9, Color(1.0, 0.8, 0.5, 0.85))
+	# The pulse: his ring flaring, then the golden shockwave.
+	if special == "pulse" and _sp < PULSE_WINDUP:
+		_over.draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, length * (0.5 + 0.2 * _sp / PULSE_WINDUP), 0, TAU, 64, Color(GOLD, 0.3 + 0.5 * _sp / PULSE_WINDUP), 8.0, true)
+	if _pulse_r >= 0.0:
+		var fade := 1.0 - _pulse_r / PULSE_REACH
+		_over.draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, _pulse_r, 0, TAU, 128, Color(GOLD, 0.15 * fade), 60.0, true)
+		_over.draw_arc(Vector2.ZERO, _pulse_r, 0, TAU, 128, Color(GOLD.lightened(0.3), 0.8 * fade), 6.0, true)
+	# The rush's path, following you while he winds up (brighter just before he goes).
+	if _rush >= 0.0 and _rush < RUSH_WINDUP:
+		var dir := _rush_dir.rotated(-global_rotation)
+		var locked := _rush >= RUSH_WINDUP * 0.75   # (brighter just before he goes)
+		var reach := RUSH_SPEED * RUSH_TIME
+		var col := Color(1.0, 0.25, 0.15, 0.55 if locked else 0.2 + 0.25 * _rush / RUSH_WINDUP)
+		_over.draw_line(dir * length * 0.4, dir * reach, Color(col, col.a * 0.35), 70.0, true)
+		_over.draw_line(dir * length * 0.4, dir * reach, col, 4.0, true)
+		var tip := dir * reach
+		_over.draw_colored_polygon(PackedVector2Array([tip + dir * 40.0, tip + dir.orthogonal() * 30.0, tip - dir.orthogonal() * 30.0]), col)
+
+
+## Orbs in his colours, red and gold.
+func _orb(vel: Vector2, col: Color) -> Orb:
+	var o := super(vel * (1.35 if phase == 2 else 1.0), col)
+	o.color = RED if col == ORB_COLOR else GOLD
+	o.global_position = eye(orbs_fired % 2)   # (each eye in turn)

+
+## On the body, in art px: the eyes and the crest gem glowing (blazing as he
+## winds up), and a trail of red light behind him while he rushes.
+func _draw_fx() -> void:
+	var charge := _charge()

+
+func _draw() -> void:

+animatable parts - the picture itself, every line, shape and colour kept.

+enclosed areas it dropped (the starfield inside the gold ring, the gems) are
+put back unless they're the pure-black background; each arm and the kicking
+leg are cut from the body along polygons traced on the art - the red cape
+behind them stays with the body - each running OVERLAP px under the body at its
+joint, so swinging them never opens a gap. Also written: a cape mask (where the
+red cape is, softened) that shaders/minotaur_cape.gdshader ripples.
+
+  data/sprites/monster_minotaur_{body,left_arm,right_arm,left_leg}.png
+  data/masks/monster_minotaur_cape.png  the cape mask
+  data/sprites/monster_minotaur.json   crop origins, pivots, eyes, crest gem

+
+

+    # softened so the ripple fades in from where it hangs.
+    cape = red & body & ((xx < 330) | (xx > 980) | ((yy > 640) & (xx < 460)))

+    bw, bh = Image.open(os.path.join(OUT, "monster_minotaur_body.png")).size

+import os
+

+import numpy as np
+from PIL import Image
+

+OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "sprites")

+    "region": [(250, 380), (480, 330), (560, 300), (612, 292), (668, 378), (610, 650), (240, 650)],
+    "shoulder": (636, 330), "elbow": (548, 372), "cut": [(500, 300), (595, 445)],
+}
+RIGHT = {
+    "region": [(1290, 380), (1100, 340), (1000, 300), (950, 292), (900, 380), (960, 650), (1300, 650)],
+    "shoulder": (936, 335), "elbow": (1040, 392), "cut": [(1085, 320), (990, 465)],
+}
+EYES = [(775, 340), (829, 345)]
+MOUTH = (800, 386)
+TENTACLE_HUB = (790, 690)

+# the hub is 210 px below the crown's gem and the tentacles span 1480 px, the
+# body (earring to earring) 1.13x the size it is here; so in this art's pixels
+# the hub sits 186 px below the gem (800, 322) and the tentacles are 1.19x.

+TENTACLE_SCALE = 1.19

+    rgba = np.array(remove(im, session=new_session("isnet-anime")))

+    cv2.fillPoly(m, [np.array(pts, np.int32)], 1)
